The change has one problem. The duplicate-guest check doesn't enforce the "once a day" rule that its error message and test name describe.

At `src/booking/commands/create_booking.rs:66-70`, the check is `existing.guest == input.guest && existing.slot == input.slot`. `Slot` has both `day` and `start` (see `seven()` in the tests), so `existing.slot == input.slot` only matches when the start time is also the same.

`bookings_on(input.slot.day)` already limits the list to that day. The extra slot comparison means a guest who has a 19:00 booking can still book 21:00 on the same day. The message ("already has a booking that day") and the test `a_guest_may_book_once_a_day` both describe a per-day limit. The test only covers the identical-slot case, so it doesn't catch this. I did not open the `Slot` definition or run the tests; this comes from how `seven()` builds a `Slot`.
